solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: There's one doctor left in the doctor's game

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written; it wraps the pieces before it
the Roman numeral for one
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
the standard abbreviation for left
to doctor results is to rig or fix them

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a lone doctor has been left inside some doctor's game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' appears twice with two different jobs: first the medical degree, then the verb meaning to fix dishonestly. 'There's' at the start is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Thimblerig is the old swindling sleight-of-hand game of guessing which of three cups hides a pea.

clue.text: Walk unsteadily with rum in bottle? Not half!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
not half means only one half of the word survives

parts.note: taken as written, then its first half goes
rum is British slang for strange, odd

explanation.surface: A drinker staggers about after downing rum from the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but it is the adjective meaning odd; ODD sits inside TLE, the back half of bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk with short unsteady steps like a small child.

clue.text: Sculpture is visible in trendy church

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: a thing visible in somewhere is seen inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sculpture is on display in a fashionable church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sculpture' must be read as a verb, to carve.
explanation.definitionFit: To incise is to cut or engrave into a surface, so to sculpt or carve.

clue.text: Expect everyone assumed reindeer comes after Nijinsky?

indicators.note: a word that has assumed another has taken it on board, holding it inside

parts.note: to bet on something is to expect it
all means everyone
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who follows the famous Nijinsky, with a reindeer joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancer is among Santa's reindeer in 'Twas the Night Before Christmas'. The question mark marks Nijinsky as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaslav Nijinsky was the celebrated Ballets Russes performer, a famous example of the profession.

clue.text: Part of corn primarily needed to make bread

parts.note: an ear is the grain-bearing head of a corn plant

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the leading letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of needed

explanation.surface: A baker's note that part of the grain is needed for bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, not the loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, so making bread is earning a living.

clue.text: Being drunk Republican is enticed to be thus?

definitions.text: Being drunk Republican is enticed to be thus?

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering and confusion, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy Republican politician is lured into a careless slip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone drunk and tempted is likely to be careless in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiscreet means unwise in speech or conduct, the state a drunk who has been lured on might fall into.

clue.text: It's hard in prison for a detective

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the word for a jail

parts.note: can is slang for prison
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Being locked up is tough on a police detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chan is the fictional Honolulu police detective of Earl Derr Biggers's novels and many films.

clue.text: Wanting opening? Cut a bit of light white wood

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: shorn means cut, as hair or fleece
a beam is a ray or shaft of light

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint about cutting a fragment of pale timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting opening' applies to 'Cut' which follows it, despite the question mark between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornbeam is a tree whose very hard pale timber is known as white wood.

clue.text: Honeymooner's want is to go around with extremely lovely wife

indicators.note: to go around means to surround the following pieces

parts.note: a want is a need
W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremities, the outer letters only

parts.note: the first and last letters of lovely
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A newly married person's wish is to go about with a lovely spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymooner is someone just married, on the holiday after the wedding.

clue.text: Type of chemical rich and idle do when tripping?

indicators.note: tripping means stumbling or being high on drugs, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sneer at what the idle rich get up to on hallucinogens.
explanation.definitionFit: A dichloride is a compound with two chlorine atoms per molecule, one kind of chemical.

clue.text: Boast about a lot of stuff

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to stuff or cram a space is to crowd it

explanation.surface: Someone brags about owning a great deal of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here is a link meaning concerning; the wordplay is the shortened verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast triumphantly, as a cockerel crows.

clue.text: Trouser pockets are dirty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally, where pockets on trousers sit on the body
second meaning: an unfair, foul blow or remark

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical location rather than a synonym, the second is the boxing idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A low blow in boxing is foul, so the idiom means unsporting or unfair, dirty play.

clue.text: Leant over and put something on ebay?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tilted, as a ship leans to one side
second meaning: offered an item for sale on an auction site

explanation.surface: Someone bends over the computer to sell an item online.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has listed has heeled over, and an item listed is posted up for sale.

clue.text: Criminal may bless court

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or lawless, so these letters are set out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer may give a blessing to the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A court in the sense of a royal court is a gathering of people, an assembly.

clue.text: Wily American actress has time for gentle old comedian

indicators.note: has ... for means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: Meryl Streep, the American actress
T is the abbreviation for time
p is piano, softly or gently in music
Ernie Wise of the British double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A crafty Hollywood star makes time for a gentle veteran comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the P in Meryl Streep's surname for T. Ernie Wise was half of Morecambe and Wise, a much-loved British comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Streetwise means shrewd and savvy in dealing with urban life, close to cunning.

clue.text: Stop to make a speech about international decline

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joined pieces go round the single letter

parts.note: to deter is to stop or discourage
to orate is to deliver a speech
I is a standard abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A call to halt and give a talk about global decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To deteriorate is to worsen or go downhill, which is what decline means as a verb.

clue.text: Nasty insult about gold vessel

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece
nasty suggests something twisted and spoilt, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A nasty remark about a golden ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nautilus is Captain Nemo's submarine, and the name of the first nuclear submarine, so a vessel.

clue.text: European requires raincoat to go out

indicators.note: to go out suggests being undone or disturbed, so the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A European needs a waterproof to step outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croatian is a person from Croatia, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Order a contract

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the way things are laid out or ordered
second meaning: an agreement settled between parties

explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement is both a tidy ordering of things and a deal made between people.

clue.text: Maintain bishop must imprison Duchess immediately, say

indicators.note: imprisoning something means locking it inside

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
D is the abbreviation for duchess

explanation.surface: Insistence that a bishop lock up a duchess at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediately is one example of the part of speech that modifies verbs.

clue.text: A sort of bench or perch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a high-backed wooden seat
second meaning: to come to rest, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Choosing between a kind of seat and a roost.
explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a long wooden bench with a high back, and to settle is to alight or come to rest.

clue.text: Burlesque? Go without an item of underwear

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: a go at something is a try
the indefinite article
a vest is an undershirt in British English

explanation.surface: A music-hall show where someone goes out without their undershirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but here it means outside. A vest is a British undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque mocking imitation, which is what a burlesque is.

clue.text: American discovered in plot with the foreign official

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it

parts.note: a garden plot is a flower bed
A is a standard abbreviation for American
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An American is uncovered in a conspiracy with a foreign official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' tempts as a scheme; it is the garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle is a minor parish or ceremonial officer, so an official.

clue.text: Flower spotted in Heidelberg

indicators.note: something spotted in a word can be seen sitting within it

parts.note: letters five to eight of the German city

explanation.surface: A bloom seen growing in a German university town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword-speak for a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elbe is a major German river, and in crosswords a flower is a thing that flows.

clue.text: Den left with strain

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for left
a strain is a tune or melody, an air

explanation.surface: A den is abandoned, leaving tension behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den or a hiding place.

clue.text: Perhaps shot put incomplete cricketer against opening

indicators.note: incomplete means lacking its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a fielder is a cricketer on the fielding side
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A cricketer half-ready stands against an opening, perhaps putting the shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' simply places the opening beside the cricketer; it is not V here.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot put is an athletics event held on the field rather than the track, an example of the category.

clue.text: Almost blacken pipe

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to singe is to scorch and blacken

explanation.surface: Nearly scorch your tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe is to sing in a high voice, as a bird pipes its song.

clue.text: Tasty Celt with 22 changes

indicators.note: changes means the combined letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 22 across

explanation.surface: A tasty Celt alters along with someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means delicious or very pleasing, a synonym for tasty.
